vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: dlazy-banana2
Version: 1.0.5

The skill is a legitimate wrapper for the dLazy CLI tool (@dlazy/cli) used for image generation via the Nano Banana 2.0 model. It follows standard SaaS patterns, requiring an API key stored in ~/.dlazy/config.json and uploading local media to oss.dlazy.com for processing. The instructions for the AI agent are focused on error handling (e.g., insufficient balance or missing API keys) and do not contain any malicious prompt injections or unauthorized data exfiltration commands.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only thin CLI wrapper for the dLazy image-generation service; its requirements and instructions are consistent with that purpose, but you should review the upstream npm/GitHub package and be aware it will use your dLazy API key and upload media to dlazy's servers.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Nano Banana 2.0 image generation) aligns with the declared requirements: npm/npx and the @dlazy/cli npm package. The skill is a thin client over dLazy's API and does not request unrelated services. Minor provenance inconsistency: the SKILL header shows version 1.0.3, registry lists 1.0.5, while the install pin in metadata uses @dlazy/cli@1.0.6 — this is a bookkeeping/versioning mismatch but does not change the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the dlazy CLI and to provide an API key via dlazy auth or DLAZY_API_KEY; it explicitly states local files passed as inputs will be uploaded to oss.dlazy.com. The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated files or credentials beyond the CLI config or the optional env var. The skill includes specific agent behaviors (e.g., inform users on insufficient balance) which are prescriptive but within scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is enforced by the registry (instruction-only), but metadata recommends installing a pinned npm package or using npx. Installing via npx/npm will fetch code from the public npm registry — appropriate for this use case but you should review the package/source (GitHub repo) before installing or prefer npx to avoid a global install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry does not require any environment variables, and the skill only references a service-specific API key (DLAZY_API_KEY) and a user config file (~/.dlazy/config.json) for storing the key. That level of access (one service key saved to the user's config) is proportional to a cloud image-generation CLI.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true (with normal autonomous invocation allowed) — standard for skills. The skill does not request permanent platform-level presence or attempt to modify other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or running this skill:
- Review the upstream GitHub repository and the @dlazy/cli npm package to confirm the code matches your expectations (the SKILL metadata pins 1.0.6 but other version fields differ). 
- Prefer running with npx (npx @dlazy/cli@1.0.6 ...) instead of a global npm -g install if you don't want to persist a binary. 
- Understand the privacy/billing implications: the CLI uploads any local images you pass to oss.dlazy.com and sends prompts to api.dlazy.com; usage will consume credits on your dLazy account. 
- Know where your API key will be stored (~/.dlazy/config.json) and that the key can also be supplied via DLAZY_API_KEY. Keep that key secret and rotate/revoke via the dLazy dashboard if needed. 
- If you are uncomfortable trusting the npm package or the dLazy service, do not install/run the CLI from this skill.
